abstract: Tomei, Klein, and Teeselink introduce a novel AI occupational exposure measure based on reinforcement learning (RL) benchmark performance rather than large language model capabilities. The authors construct an RL Feasibility Index by scoring all 17,951 O*NET tasks across 894 U.S. occupations on eight dimensions reflecting RL environment feasibility: verification method, environment simulability, state observability, task variability, sequential depth, feedback density, tool accessibility, and output tangibility. Tasks requiring substantial physical embodiment receive zero scores via a physical feasibility gate. The resulting exposure patterns diverge meaningfully from LLM-based indices — the two measures correlate at 0.88 overall but only 0.15 among digitally feasible tasks. Top RL-exposed occupations include data entry keyers (71.0), correspondence clerks (68.6), and proofreaders (68.6) — primarily digital, rule-governed roles with verifiable outputs. RL exposure shows a hump-shaped relationship with wages, peaking in upper-middle deciles and lowest among highest and lowest earners, echoing middle-class erosion patterns from prior automation waves. A difference-in-differences analysis of job postings finds occupations with higher RL exposure experienced approximately 2.9% relative declines in openings post-ChatGPT, with effects accelerating over time.
keyFindings: RL-based and LLM-based AI exposure indices correlate at 0.88 overall but only 0.15 among digitally feasible tasks, revealing fundamentally different exposure patterns
Top RL-exposed occupations are digital, rule-governed roles: data entry keyers (71.0), correspondence clerks (68.6), proofreaders (68.6)
RL exposure follows a hump-shaped wage relationship, peaking in upper-middle deciles — echoing middle-class erosion patterns from prior automation waves
Monitoring/control roles (railroad conductors, gas plant operators) show high RL but low LLM exposure due to verifiable outcomes and discrete action spaces
Difference-in-differences analysis finds 2.9% relative decline in job postings for high RL-exposure occupations post-ChatGPT, with accelerating effects
methodology: LLM-based annotation (Gemini 2.5 Flash) guided by expert-developed rubric to score 17,951 O*NET tasks on 8 RL feasibility dimensions across 894 occupations. Physical feasibility gate filters embodied tasks. Difference-in-differences analysis of job posting data (August 2021 - November 2025) to validate labor market effects. Importance-weighted aggregation from task to occupation level.
qualifiers: LLM-based task annotation introduces potential measurement error and annotator model biases. RL feasibility is a theoretical construct — actual RL deployment may not follow predicted exposure patterns. Job posting analysis captures demand-side effects but not actual employment changes. The physical feasibility gate may become less relevant as robotics capabilities advance. Exposure measure reflects current RL capabilities and may not predict future exposure accurately.
